title: Fly learning and circuit computation: source-audited operational catalogue
provenance: New research; not recovery or reconstruction of the missing original
scope: Adult Drosophila; explicitly labeled larval/preprint evidence; separate fixed computations from learning

entries.name: Population normalization with spatially local inhibition
entries.evidence: Shown: antennal-lobe inhibition produces divisive normalization; APL inhibition within the mushroom body can be spatially localized. These are convergent examples of normalization, not two independent general learning algorithms. The localized APL result specifically argues against equating the entire biological circuit with one global scalar.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: sensory afferents excite projection neurons and recruit inhibitory local neurons; in the mushroom body, KCs recruit APL and receive inhibition. Use positive drive and negative inhibitory feedback. The exact pooling neighborhood is architecture, not a universal biological convergence ratio.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes pooling neighborhoods and gains; lifetime activity varies without requiring weight learning. Proposed rate approximation: pool_p = sum of locally connected activities; output_i = drive_i / (epsilon + gain * pool_p). A neuronal pooling unit supplies the denominator, rather than a synapse reading the whole network.
entries.scaling: H = O(1–10) gains per pooling class; activity state O(N+P), edges O(S_pool), work O(S_pool) per update. Explicit pooling adjacency still occupies storage. Learned normalization weights would add S_pool independent parameters; they are not included for free.
entries.models: Olsen et al. (2010) fitted a normalization computation to odor-response measurements. Amin et al. (2020) constrained the spatial implementation. Neither establishes locally learned semantic routing; no separately verified implementation package is claimed here.
entries.buy: Gain robustness and controlled competition, not discovery of an arithmetic rule. Local rather than global pooling could preserve several concurrent representations.
entries.overlap: Already-covered inhibition/sparsity family. The September ledger records scalar APL work; local neighborhoods are a variant, not a newly discovered family.
entries.minimal_test: Local versus global pooling, with equal edge/state budget, training and updates. Measurement: held-out accuracy under input gain variation.
entries.confidence: High for normalization; medium for transferring the spatially local variant to MiniFly.
entries.local_sufficiency: Fixed computation; learning sufficiency not applicable.
entries.verification_status: Convergent computational role across two circuits; no claim of independent replication of the complete proposed MiniFly motif.

entries.name: Adaptive temporal filtering
entries.evidence: Shown: fly olfactory receptor responses have adaptive temporal dynamics, and spike generation adds temporal filtering. This supports a computation over recent history; it does not show durable rule learning.
entries.wiring: Adult fly olfactory receptor neurons transform sensory drive before projection-neuron and KC processing. A compact abstraction uses a local slow state that subtracts from current excitation.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes time constants and filter signs. Proposed local state rule: a_next = (1-alpha)*a + alpha*x; output = phi(x - beta*a). This is activity-state adaptation, not a weight update. Do not relabel every adaptation time constant as a separate mechanism.
entries.scaling: H = O(1–10) per cell class; O(N) adaptive state and work for one filter per channel. K time constants require O(KN) state even if coefficients are shared.
entries.models: Nagel & Wilson (2011), Nature Neuroscience: dynamical account of odor-driven responses. It explains temporal response structure, not symbolic transfer.
entries.buy: Can suppress persistent nuisance drive while preserving transients; can also erase a sustained cue that matters. It does not solve format invariance without a suitable coding relation.
entries.overlap: The historical ledger already contains temporal-contrast/fast-minus-slow sensory variants. This is a source-grounded reference, not an untested recommendation.
entries.minimal_test: Adaptive filter versus an equal-state fixed filter, both with matched downstream learning. Measurement: held-out accuracy when only nuisance stimulus persistence changes.
entries.confidence: High for temporal filtering; conditional for task usefulness.
entries.local_sufficiency: Fixed computation; learning sufficiency not applicable.
entries.verification_status: One primary mechanistic study selected; independent replication not established by this review.

entries.name: Learned inhibition of familiar background
entries.evidence: Shown/inferred: targeted experiments implicate local inhibitory plasticity in odor-specific habituation. This differs from F02: the relevant effective inhibition changes with experience rather than merely tracking a fast adaptation state. A complete synapse-by-synapse learning equation was not measured. Sudhakaran et al. (2012) provides a follow-up dissection of recurrent inhibitory pathways, but is not independent replication by a wholly separate research group.
entries.wiring: Adult fly antennal lobe: projection neurons interact with GABAergic local interneurons that suppress odor responses. Represent the plastic inhibitory connection as a nonnegative magnitude with an explicitly negative output sign.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes partners. A proposed, not experimentally identified, inhibitory update is: delta inhibitory_magnitude = eta * local_presynaptic_activity * (target_activity - target_rate). It increases inhibition when the target is too active. A familiarity/exposure gate must be locally supplied if used; semantic irrelevance cannot be assumed.
entries.scaling: H = O(1–10); S_I plastic inhibitory magnitudes plus O(N) rate state, O(S_I) work. Sharing all magnitudes by type would remove the specificity that makes this useful.
entries.models: Das et al. (2011), PNAS: circuit manipulations and behavioral habituation. The proposed rate-target rule here is an engineering candidate, not a reproduction of the animal mechanism.
entries.buy: Could reduce interference from repeated formatting or background cues. Failure mode: suppressing a frequent but essential operand or delimiter.
entries.overlap: Overlaps inhibitory adaptation and existing input-side plasticity. No claim that a particular MiniFly implementation is untested.
entries.minimal_test: Adaptive inhibitory weights versus frozen equal-size inhibitory weights. Measurement: retained task accuracy after exposure to a repeated, task-irrelevant background.
entries.confidence: Medium: causal circuit evidence is stronger than knowledge of the update rule.
entries.local_sufficiency: Unknown for the biological task under the proposed rule; unestablished for MiniFly.
entries.verification_status: Primary study plus targeted follow-up from overlapping research lineage; not an independent replication claim.

entries.name: Input-side timing-dependent plasticity
entries.evidence: Shown: timing-dependent changes at incoming PN→KC synapses can facilitate olfactory learning, with dopaminergic involvement. This is not merely KC→MBON valence writing at the output. It supplies a specific alternative locus for adapting representations.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: excitatory projection-neuron input reaches KC dendrites; dopaminergic signals modulate input plasticity. Keep the anatomical site separate from downstream KC→MBON writes.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes sparse partners; lifetime PN→KC magnitudes are plastic. Proposed abstraction: delta w_ij = eta * local_timing_kernel(pre_i, post_j) * local_modulator_j, followed by sign-preserving bounds. The paper supports timing sensitivity, not this exact universal factorization or a particular numerical kernel.
entries.scaling: H = O(10) kernel/gain parameters; S_in independent weights and O(S_in) eligibility if traces are synapse-specific. A neuron-shared trace can reduce storage only when the chosen rule permits it.
entries.models: Qiao et al. (2022), Current Biology: recordings and olfactory-learning experiments. No verified general byte-learning code or demonstrated abstract-rule induction is supplied by that study.
entries.buy: Could retune a representation instead of continually overwriting its readout. It might improve salience and sample efficiency, but also destabilize old readout meanings.
entries.overlap: Explicitly present as ITDP/M10 in the September pruning ledger. Keep as a mechanistically specified variant, not a newly found idea.
entries.minimal_test: Input-plastic versus input-frozen encoders, matched in storage and downstream updates. Measurement: old-format held-out accuracy after learning the new format.
entries.confidence: Medium: identified plastic site and timing effect; algorithmic sufficiency unresolved.
entries.local_sufficiency: Partial: a local plastic site is supported; end-to-end sufficiency is not.
entries.verification_status: One primary causal/physiological study selected; independent replication not established here.

entries.name: Timing-sensitive, signed associative writing
entries.evidence: Shown: odor-linked KC→MBON plasticity can be induced by appropriately timed dopamine, and timing can change the sign of the resulting association/plasticity. These findings justify a timing-sensitive local teaching mechanism. They do not establish a universal pre×post×dopamine rule at every such synapse.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: cholinergic KCs excite MBONs; compartmental DANs modulate the KC→MBON connections. The teaching input is not the same thing as an excitatory postsynaptic current.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes compartments; life changes individual KC→MBON magnitudes. Proposed abstraction: eligibility_next = lambda*eligibility + local_activity_event; delta w = eta*eligibility*signed_local_teaching_signal. A timing kernel or opponent teaching channels determine sign. The effective predictor update must be translated consistently into depression/potentiation of an excitatory physical synapse.
entries.scaling: H = O(1–10) per compartment class; S_w plastic weights and up to S_w eligibility traces. Work O(S_active) with sparse events, otherwise O(S_w). Long-lived capture state is additional, not synonymous with eligibility.
entries.models: Hige et al. (2015) and Handler et al. (2019) provide experimental constraints. Bennett et al. (2021; F08) shows one computational use of prediction-driven MB plasticity, not a proof that this generic rule solves arbitrary tasks.
entries.buy: Delayed local credit and rapid associations. A scalar reward plus eligibility does not by itself identify which hidden representation should be changed to generalize.
entries.overlap: Baseline/retained family: local writing and eligibility already exist in the historical project. Synaptic tagging, eligibility and consolidation should not be counted as synonyms or automatically as three new modules.
entries.minimal_test: Timed eligibility versus a shuffled-time, equal-storage eligibility control. Measurement: prediction accuracy at a fixed cue-to-reward delay.
entries.confidence: High for timing-dependent associative plasticity; low for inferring general rule learning from it.
entries.local_sufficiency: Partial; sufficient for specified simple associative models, not established for the target learner.
entries.verification_status: Convergent primary studies of local plasticity and timing; exact equations differ and are not collapsed into one measured rule.

entries.name: Compartment-specific teaching channels
entries.evidence: Shown: adult DAN cell types write and update memories with different dynamics. Larval connectomics and modeling show substantial recurrent organization around teaching neurons. This supports heterogeneous teaching channels; it does not establish independent, arbitrary target vectors for every neuron.
entries.wiring: Adult: distinct DAN projections modulate different KC→MBON compartments. Larval evidence supplies additional recurrent motifs but is explicitly cross-stage evidence. Connection signs must be specified per selected motif, not inferred from the word dopamine.
entries.algorithm: Development sets the routing matrix and a small number C of channel types. Proposed lifetime update: delta w_ic = eta_c * e_ic * d_c. Each d_c must be computed by its local circuit from allowed inputs. C independent external target errors are not silently equivalent to one scalar reward.
entries.scaling: H = O(C) rule coefficients, potentially O(C²) intercompartment couplings; O(S_w) plastic weights and traces. Scaling C with width increases teaching bandwidth and must be reported.
entries.models: Aso & Rubin (2016) supplies cell-type-specific learning constraints. Eschbach et al. (2020), Nature Neuroscience, combines larval recurrent anatomy and computational analysis; biological wiring alone does not certify all training operations as local.
entries.buy: Could specialize where credit is delivered and separate stable from flexible channels. It need not improve composition unless useful information reaches the appropriate channel.
entries.overlap: Already-covered compartment heterogeneity/teaching allocation. More compartments are not automatically new mechanisms.
entries.minimal_test: Compartment-targeted versus channel-permuted modulation, matching modulator amplitudes and all state. Measurement: held-out loss after conflicting teaching events.
entries.confidence: High for heterogeneity; medium for a chosen routing abstraction.
entries.local_sufficiency: Partial: local modulation exists; sufficiency of learned routing remains task-dependent.
entries.verification_status: Adult cell-type evidence plus larval architecture/model evidence; cross-stage convergence is not adult replication.
entries.species_stage: Adult Drosophila melanogaster; F06 additionally labels larval evidence explicitly.

entries.name: Activity-dependent amplification of teaching
entries.evidence: Shown: reciprocal KC–DAN connectivity includes a positive feedback contribution required for learning. This is an amplification loop, not evidence that the loop subtracts an expected reward.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: KCs provide excitatory cholinergic feedback to DANs; DANs modulate KC output synapses. These are different signal types around the loop.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes feedback weights and saturation. Proposed dynamics: d_next = clip(external_teaching + gain*sum(local_KC_activity), 0, d_max). Lifetime KC→MBON plasticity remains F05. A learned feedback matrix would be another plastic site requiring its own rule.
entries.scaling: H = O(1–10) gain/decay/bound parameters, O(C) DAN state and O(S_feedback) edges/work. Feedback adjacency and any independent feedback weights must be counted.
entries.models: Cervantes-Sandoval et al. (2017), eLife: structural/functional intervention evidence. No verified stand-alone byte learner or policy-gradient equivalence is claimed.
entries.buy: Could improve salience-dependent write strength or credit delivery with weak teaching. Positive feedback can instead amplify noise and unrelated writes.
entries.overlap: Overlaps the retained MB output/teaching loop. Do not conflate this operation with the error subtraction in F08 or the transfer of teacher status in F09.
entries.minimal_test: Closed loop versus activity-independent, gain-matched teaching. Measurement: examples needed for a fixed trained-association accuracy.
entries.confidence: Medium: supported circuit motif; useful gain schedule is task-specific.
entries.local_sufficiency: Partial; local components are available, global sufficiency not established.
entries.verification_status: One selected primary circuit study; no independent replication claim.

entries.name: Prediction-error computation in an MB output–teaching loop
entries.evidence: Proposed and tested in models: output-neuron predictions feed back to dopamine-like teaching signals, allowing error-driven rather than absolute-reinforcement updates. Conditioning and blocking simulations are evidence for the model’s behavior, not direct proof that all fly DANs implement this calculation.
entries.wiring: Model: KC activity drives output predictions; effective feedback opposes external reinforcement at teaching units. Positive and negative signals require opponent/sign-constrained pathways rather than an unexplained negative dopamine concentration.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes circuit signs/routing; life changes effective predictor weights. Minimal local model: prediction = sum_i(v_i*x_i); delta = reward - prediction; e_i_next = lambda*e_i + x_i; delta v_i = eta*delta*e_i. The target/output orientation determines the corresponding physical KC→MBON update sign. No hidden-layer gradient follows from this equation.
entries.scaling: H = O(1–10) per channel; S predictor weights, up to S traces, O(S) work. A single output can use scalar error; many outputs need specified local/error routing, not uncounted supervision.
entries.models: Bennett, Philippides & Nowotny (2021), Nature Communications: explicit constrained/augmented models and released simulation code. Fits multiple associative-learning phenomena; some explanatory connectivity is postulated. Code existence verified; not rerun here.
entries.buy: Prediction calibration and reduced unnecessary writes once a consequence is predicted. Useful for sample efficiency; not a solution to latent-variable discovery or symbolic compositionality.
entries.overlap: Potentially an already implemented teacher-quality mechanism. The exact current MiniFly feedback computation has not been re-audited in this review.
entries.minimal_test: Prediction-error feedback versus absolute teaching with matched update norm and state budget. Measurement: asymptotic consequence-prediction error.
entries.confidence: High for the stated computational result; medium/low for the full biological interpretation.
entries.local_sufficiency: Yes in the published model’s specified associative tasks; unknown for MiniFly transfer.
entries.verification_status: Published computational task demonstrations and verified code availability; not experimental replication of biological RPE computation.

entries.name: A learned cue becomes a teacher for another association
entries.evidence: Shown: second-order conditioning uses a hierarchy in which a learned reward-predicting cue can recruit teaching for another compartment. Rachad et al. (2025) supplies convergent circuit/behavioral/model evidence for higher-order associative chains. This is stronger than merely observing anatomical recurrence, but remains distinct from learning a reusable arithmetic operation.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: a relatively stable teacher compartment influences faster student compartments through an excitatory intermediary; additional experiments identify excitatory and inhibitory feedback around dopaminergic signaling. Avoid treating all routes as one universal fixed diagram.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes teacher→intermediary→student routes. Proposed abstraction: d_student = external_reward + alpha*teacher_output; delta w_student = eta*student_eligibility*d_student. Teacher output must be learned from experience, not supplied from labels at test time. The full biological update and safeguards against self-reinforcing false predictions remain incompletely identified.
entries.scaling: H = O(C) channel gains and time constants, O(S_teacher+S_student) plastic state, plus bounded intermediary state. Dense teacher–student connectivity costs O(C²); sparse hierarchy O(C).
entries.models: Yamada et al. (2023), eLife: anatomical/physiological/behavioral work with modeling. Rachad et al. (2025), Cell Reports: circuit dissection plus computational modeling. A public reusable model-code package was not verified here; anatomical viewer links are not model code.
entries.buy: Composes learned associations without direct primary reward for every link. This supports an operational teaching-transfer hypothesis, not a claim of zero-shot algebra.
entries.overlap: Subfamily of existing MB feedback and fast/slow compartments, but teaching transfer is an identifiable extra operation. Current exact implementation status unknown.
entries.minimal_test: Learned teacher output versus equal-amplitude shuffled teacher output, after identical first-order training. Measurement: second-order cue preference without primary reward to that cue.
entries.confidence: Medium–high for associative chaining; low for extrapolation to general rule induction.
entries.local_sufficiency: Partial: task-level circuit/model evidence; no general sufficiency theorem.
entries.verification_status: Two primary circuit studies from different research groups support higher-order association; they are convergent, not identical-protocol replications.

entries.name: State-dependent readout and disinhibitory routing
entries.evidence: Shown: motivational state can gate memory expression, and learning/motivation can alter feed-forward inhibition in the MB output network. Failure to express a behavior is therefore not automatically loss of the stored association.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: state-related signals influence dopaminergic/MB circuits; inhibitory MBON pathways regulate other output pathways. An inhibitory neuron suppressing an inhibitory route can disinhibit the selected output.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes routes. Proposed readout: output = g(state)*memory_output, with a small fixed state-to-gain map; a more explicit version uses two inhibitory stages. The evidence does not specify a generally sufficient local rule for learning arbitrary context keys. Changing state can alter reads without changing stored weights.
entries.scaling: H = O(C) gains for fixed state channels, O(C+N) activity. Learning a context router adds S_gate weights and its local learning state; do not count only the final gain.
entries.models: Krashes et al. (2009), Cell, and Perisse et al. (2016), Neuron: causal circuit/behavioral constraints. Neither is a demonstration of locally trained transformer-style keys.
entries.buy: Could separate storage from access and prevent irrelevant context from determining the output. It offers a hypothesis for format-dependent access failures, not proof that E16 is an access failure.
entries.overlap: Existing internal-state gating family and overlaps the separate attention/WM survey. No new generic “add a gate” recommendation.
entries.minimal_test: State-sensitive readout versus state-permuted readout, holding all stored association weights fixed at evaluation. Measurement: recovery of old-format accuracy.
entries.confidence: High for state-dependent expression; low for arbitrary learned routing sufficiency.
entries.local_sufficiency: Fixed gate is straightforward; learning the correct gate is unestablished.
entries.verification_status: Convergent behavioral/circuit studies; does not establish an arbitrary learned router.

entries.name: Opposing learned memories rather than overwriting one trace
entries.evidence: Shown: extinction can involve a parallel opposing memory that competes with the original association. This is not the claim that all forgetting is erasure or that every inhibitory response is a separate memory system.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: distinct MB pathways preserve and oppose learned valence, converging on behavioral output. Keep route-specific excitation/inhibition separate from the sign of the net learned preference.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes two opposing channels. Proposed effective output: value = original_prediction - opponent_prediction. Both channels can use bounded locally modulated associative updates; omitted expected reinforcement trains the opponent only if that omission signal is explicitly computed. This equation is an abstraction, not the measured complete biological rule.
entries.scaling: H = O(1–10); approximately 2S associative weights if both channels have S edges, plus traces if used. Parameter sharing does not remove the second stored trace.
entries.models: Felsenberg et al. (2018), Cell: circuit and behavioral evidence for parallel opposing memory. No claim that a generic two-head implementation reproduces every extinction phenomenon.
entries.buy: Revision with potential recovery of old behavior instead of irreversible replacement. It can reduce one kind of forgetting but does not discover invariant input representations.
entries.overlap: Overlaps banks, compartmental retention and revision already screened. Include as a mechanistic distinction, not another broad memory-management proposal.
entries.minimal_test: Opponent trace versus single-trace updating under equal total writable storage. Measurement: old-association recovery after removal of the extinction context.
entries.confidence: High for the reported extinction mechanism; conditional for format-transfer failures.
entries.local_sufficiency: Partial: local implementation plausible; particular rule must be demonstrated.
entries.verification_status: One selected primary circuit study; no claim of universal extinction mechanism.

entries.name: Bounded post-event teaching reverberation
entries.evidence: Shown/inferred: recurrent reward-related activity contributes to appetitive long-term memory, while inhibitory feedback helps regulate dopaminergic activity. These studies concern different circuit details, so their combination into one controller is proposed. Matsuno et al. (2026) links aberrant post-training dopamine to maladaptive memory broadening, not useful rule generalization.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: recurrent MB–DAN signaling supplies persistence; a GABAergic feedback pathway regulates dopaminergic input. Do not assert a direct monosynaptic inhibitory edge where only a functional pathway is established.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes loop gains and negative-feedback topology. Proposed two-state controller: d_next = clip((1-a)*d + b*event - c*z,0,d_max); z_next = (1-h)*z + h*d. d gates already eligible local writes. Eligibility must decay or reset so unrelated later inputs are not captured. This is bounded teaching persistence, not an archive replay buffer.
entries.scaling: H = O(10) per channel, O(C) controller state plus existing weight/eligibility storage. K post-event updates multiply work by K even if no weights are added.
entries.models: Ichinose et al. (2015), eLife, and Pavlowsky et al. (2018), Current Biology: experimental constraints on persistence and feedback. The two-state engineering controller is proposed here, not claimed as their exact model.
entries.buy: Can extend an informative teaching event while terminating harmful indiscriminate writing. It addresses write timing; it cannot recreate missing old examples.
entries.overlap: Already-covered consolidation/termination family. Keep separate from replay but do not launch it instead of the user-described replay controls.
entries.minimal_test: Negative-feedback-terminated versus duration-matched externally truncated teaching, equal total update budget. Measurement: old-task loss after unrelated post-event inputs.
entries.confidence: Medium: component findings are strong; synthesis and transfer remain unproven.
entries.local_sufficiency: Partial; no established complete local algorithm for the MiniFly failure.
entries.verification_status: Several primary studies constrain persistence, termination and overgeneralization, but not one jointly validated controller.

entries.name: Re-anchor new sensory renderings to a stable internal coordinate
entries.evidence: Shown: the visual input associated with an internal heading representation can be reorganized by sensorimotor experience. Convergent 2019 studies connect stable heading dynamics with adaptable visual mapping. The exact synaptic learning law is inferred/proposed, not directly measured in full. A December 2025 preprint by Plitt et al. reports that octopaminergic feedback conveys heading activity to sensory presynaptic terminals and is necessary/sufficient for the tested anchoring plasticity; this newer claim remains provisional.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: visual ring-neuron input inhibits compass E-PG neurons; the compass has recurrent state-maintaining dynamics. Plastic sensory anchoring is distinguished from the recurrent dynamics that maintain the internal coordinate.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes the compass kernel; life changes sensory-to-state anchoring. Proposed inhibitory-association variant: delta a_ij = -eta*visual_i*state_j + slow_local_restoration(a_ij), with nonnegative inhibitory magnitudes. Weakening coactive inhibition can anchor the cue to the occupied state. The exact rule/bounds need validation; a privileged correct-state target is not allowed. The preprint motivates replacing direct state_j in the update by a locally delivered modulatory state signal m_j. That spatially structured feedback is not a single uniform global reward scalar and must be explicitly implemented and budgeted.
entries.scaling: H = O(10) kernel/rule parameters plus S_anchor independent anchoring weights and O(N) state. Dense M-cue by N-state anchoring costs O(MN); sparse degree-k anchoring O(kM). It is not a ten-parameter learner merely because the ring kernel has ten parameters.
entries.models: Fisher et al. (2019) and Kim et al. (2019), Nature: physiological experiments with constrained models. Kim et al. supplies an author data/code page. The task has continuous heading and sensorimotor correspondence, not arbitrary symbolic renaming.
entries.buy: A plausible analogue for separating a stable latent computation from a changing input format. It requires an observable bridge between formats; it cannot infer an arbitrary unseen permutation with no paired cues or feedback.
entries.overlap: Family overlap with input plasticity and the already-tested CX. Whether the exact sensory-anchor variant was tested is unknown; it must not be announced as new.
entries.minimal_test: Plastic versus frozen anchoring with identical recurrent core and allowed observations. Measurement: old-format accuracy after learning a second rendering of the same observable transitions.
entries.confidence: Medium–high for sensory remapping; conditional for byte-format transfer.
entries.local_sufficiency: Partial: local models exist; target-task sufficiency and unprivileged anchoring unestablished.
entries.verification_status: Two peer-reviewed 2019 studies converge on flexible anchoring; 2025 feedback mechanism is a separately labeled, unreplicated preprint.

entries.name: Continuous recurrent working state
entries.evidence: Shown/inferred through perturbation and modeling: fly heading populations have ring-attractor dynamics. This supports persistent low-dimensional state. It does not establish a locally learned general working-memory program.
entries.wiring: Adult fly central brain: E-PG-centered recurrent compass circuitry with effective excitation and inhibition maintains a localized population state. A signed ring kernel is an abstraction; negative effective couplings must be realized through inhibitory pathways.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes a translation-structured recurrent kernel. Proposed dynamics: h_next = phi(K*h + B*motion - inhibition); the stable bump encodes state. No lifetime weight changes are necessary for this computation. Sensory anchoring plasticity is F13, not evidence of a plastic ring kernel.
entries.scaling: H = O(1–10) kernel/shift parameters; O(N) activity, O(kN) work with k local neighbors or O(N²) for a naive dense kernel. Multiple independent registers multiply state and dynamics; shared coefficients do not provide free memory capacity.
entries.models: Kim et al. (2017), Science: perturbation-constrained model with released code. It explains heading-bump behavior, not arbitrary manipulation of multiple symbolic registers.
entries.buy: Persistent state and continuous integration with low shared-parameter cost. Useful only when inputs can legitimately be grounded to the state variable.
entries.overlap: Already-reviewed/tested central-complex family. Exact implementation details were not inspected here.
entries.minimal_test: Structured versus phase-scrambled recurrence, matched degree, gains, state and internal update count. Measurement: drift over a specified delay.
entries.confidence: High for the specified state dynamics; low for general program inference.
entries.local_sufficiency: Not applicable to the fixed kernel; grounding/readout learning remains separate.
entries.verification_status: Perturbation plus model in a primary paper; code verified, not independently rerun here.

entries.name: Accumulate evidence before committing
entries.evidence: Shown: subthreshold dendritic activity in αβ-core KCs integrates olfactory evidence on behaviorally relevant decision timescales. This is a within-neuron temporal computation, not evidence that recurrent weights were learned for the task.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: sensory inputs reach KC dendrites; membrane integration precedes spike/decision threshold. A simplified circuit uses excitatory evidence drive, leak and threshold/reset.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes integration/threshold parameters. Proposed state rule: z_next = (1-leak)*z + evidence; commit when z reaches threshold, then reset. A signed evidence difference requires separately specified opponent inputs. No weight plasticity is required for the accumulator.
entries.scaling: H = O(1–10) per accumulator class; O(N) state and O(S_input+N) work. K integration steps cost K updates. Arbitrary learned evidence encoders add their own weights and credit-assignment problem.
entries.models: Groschner et al. (2018), Cell: recordings, manipulations and a perceptual-decision account. The model addresses discrimination timing, not long symbolic reasoning.
entries.buy: Can integrate noisy or distributed cues and delay action until sufficient evidence accumulates. This is a different operation from storing an arbitrary item without drift.
entries.overlap: Overlap with the recurrent-state/integration family; more specific than adding a generic RNN. Current exact implementation unknown.
entries.minimal_test: Accumulator versus matched-state instantaneous decision mechanism, equal total observations and compute. Measurement: decision error at a fixed observation budget.
entries.confidence: High for evidence integration; medium for the proposed compact abstraction.
entries.local_sufficiency: Fixed computation; sufficiency of a learned encoder is unknown.
entries.verification_status: Primary recordings/manipulations with mechanistic modeling; independent replication not established here.

entries.name: Coordinate transformation by population-vector combination
entries.evidence: Shown/inferred from recordings and circuit organization: fan-shaped-body pathways combine movement-related signals to represent allocentric travelling direction. This is a coordinate transformation, not proof of a complete learned home-vector integrator or universal addition engine. Ishida et al. (2026) further shows a population-vector inversion operation associated with a change in firing mode. Inversion is recorded here as a distinct operator within the vector-computation family, not padded into another broad family.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: heading and movement signals shape PFN population phases/amplitudes; phase-shifted convergence onto hΔB-related populations combines components. Do not replace the biological arrangement with an unsupported universal eight-column ratio.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes phase offsets and coupling. Mathematical abstraction: world_vector = rotation(heading) * body_vector; a population implementation sums appropriately shifted component codes. This is a runtime operation; no local learning law is needed for fixed couplings. Learning what a raw byte denotes remains outside the circuit. For the inversion variant, the mathematical operation is v_out = -v_in, represented as a half-turn of population phase; this does not imply negative firing rates.
entries.scaling: H = O(10–100) across selected population types; O(N) population state and O(S_vector) edges/work. Dense implementations may cost O(N²); sparse columnar implementations can cost O(N). The low-dimensional formula does not eliminate neural encoding cost.
entries.models: Lyu, Abbott & Maimon (2022), Nature: circuit-linked computational account of travelling direction. It does not test locally learned modular arithmetic from arbitrary byte labels.
entries.buy: Composition of grounded transformations. Potentially useful as a computational primitive, but inserting arithmetic structure into development changes what the learner is being asked to discover.
entries.overlap: Already-reviewed/tested CX family. No novelty claim for generic vector addition.
entries.minimal_test: Correct versus permuted phase-offset circuitry with equal edges, training and update count. Measurement: coordinate-transform error on held-out trajectories.
entries.confidence: High for the reported transformation; low for arbitrary symbolic-transfer claims.
entries.local_sufficiency: Fixed computation; learning sufficiency not applicable.
entries.verification_status: Primary vector-transformation and later inversion studies; complementary operations, not replicated end-to-end learning.

entries.name: Compare current state with a goal in a common coordinate
entries.evidence: Shown: fly steering circuitry transforms heading/goal information into lateralized commands. Convergent 2024 studies identify how such comparisons can drive goal-oriented steering. Their findings do not supply a general local rule for learning all goals from sparse reward.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: compass/goal-related populations converge through fan-shaped-body/PFL pathways onto left/right steering outputs. A compact opponent readout represents signed directional error; individual biological signs are pathway-specific.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes comparison topology. Proposed abstraction: left = max(0, sin(goal-heading)); right = max(0, sin(heading-goal)). Goal is bounded activity state, not an unexplained task label. A learned goal-setting policy needs an additional local algorithm, which this comparison does not provide.
entries.scaling: H = O(10) shared couplings; O(N) activity for population codes and O(S_compare) work. A dense arbitrary goal embedding adds parameters; a formula for angular error is not itself a learned embedding.
entries.models: Mussells Pires et al. (2024) and Westeinde et al. (2024), Nature: physiological/circuit models of steering. They support the comparator, not generic planning or symbolic goals.
entries.buy: Provides an error direction for an already meaningful state space. It can support controlled iteration but does not determine what goal is correct.
entries.overlap: Part of the existing central-complex/goal family; not another independent source of generic learning capacity.
entries.minimal_test: Goal-aligned versus goal-label-permuted comparator, matching all state/compute. Measurement: angular goal error on held-out starts.
entries.confidence: High for steering comparison; conditional for nonspatial use.
entries.local_sufficiency: Not applicable to fixed comparison; learning goal selection remains unknown.
entries.verification_status: Two independent-group 2024 studies converge on steering computation; no inference of generic goal learning.

entries.name: Multiplicative interaction through excitation and disinhibition
entries.evidence: Shown with recordings and conductance-based simulation: coincident excitation and release from inhibition produce a multiplication-like nonlinearity in T4 motion neurons. This is an analogue approximation over an operating range, not exact arbitrary signed multiplication.
entries.wiring: Adult fly visual circuit: cholinergic inputs excite T4; glutamatergic Mi9 input acts inhibitory in this circuit. The interaction depends on local dendritic conductance, illustrating why transmitter identity alone is not a universal sign label.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes input placement/gains. Proposed computational abstraction: output = phi(excitatory_input) * gate(local_disinhibition). Both signals must arrive physically at the neuron. No lifetime synaptic learning is required for the interaction; learning operands or routing into it is a separate problem.
entries.scaling: H = O(1–10) gains per motif; O(N) local activity. D input pairs require O(D) interactions; an unrestricted all-pairs bilinear layer costs O(D²). Shared gains do not make all pairings free.
entries.models: Groschner et al. (2022), Nature: conductance-based model tested against visual responses and perturbations. No verified general local-rule learner follows from the model.
entries.buy: Adds an actual conjunction/gating operation rather than another memory store. Could increase representational/computational expressivity while preserving local signal access.
entries.overlap: Potentially a specific variant within the previously reviewed gain/routing family; not established as untested in MiniFly.
entries.minimal_test: Multiplicative versus additive interaction, equal input edges, states and training. Measurement: held-out accuracy on conjunctions whose components were seen separately.
entries.confidence: High for the measured interaction; medium for the useful abstraction.
entries.local_sufficiency: Fixed computation; learning to exploit it remains unestablished.
entries.verification_status: Primary physiology, perturbation and conductance model; not a demonstrated general-purpose arithmetic unit.

entries.name: Predict and cancel self-generated sensory input
entries.evidence: Shown: motor-related signals counteract expected visual consequences in fly visuomotor neurons. This supports an efference-copy/cancellation computation; it does not demonstrate a general predictive-coding learning rule.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: motor-related signals converge with sensory signals in visual processing. Their effective sign/latency offsets expected reafferent drive. The detailed origin of every cancelling pathway need not be assumed for the abstraction.
entries.algorithm: Development supplies a motor-to-sensory prediction map. Runtime: residual = sensory_input - predicted_input(action_copy). A possible lifetime adaptation delta w = eta*action_feature*local_residual is proposed, not established by the cited experiment. The residual must be present at the receiving neuron.
entries.scaling: H = O(10) for fixed low-dimensional gains; S_predict independent coefficients if the prediction map is learned, plus local trace state if delay matters. Work O(S_predict).
entries.models: Kim, Fitzgerald & Maimon (2015), Nature Neuroscience: electrophysiological evidence. No claim that this study trained a general predictive model locally.
entries.buy: Could distinguish an agent’s own output/expected feedback from external novelty. Relevant only when a causal action-feedback channel exists; subtracting predictable task signal can be harmful.
entries.overlap: Related to predictive/residual mechanisms, not a synonym for cortical backpropagation. Current exact MiniFly coverage unknown.
entries.minimal_test: Action-aligned versus shuffled-action prediction, equal prediction resources. Measurement: residual false alarms during self-generated inputs.
entries.confidence: Medium–high for cancellation; low for the general learning extension.
entries.local_sufficiency: Fixed cancellation supported; learned-map sufficiency unknown.
entries.verification_status: Primary cellular evidence; learned cancellation rule remains a proposed extension.

entries.name: Priority competition that produces a sequence
entries.evidence: Shown/inferred through perturbation: competing grooming programs are organized by suppression relationships; removal of a dominant drive allows another program to emerge. This is innate behavioral sequencing, not demonstrated learning of arbitrary routines.
entries.wiring: Adult fly: parallel sensory-to-motor programs compete through effective suppression. Use a directed inhibitory priority graph as the abstraction; the behavioral model is not a complete cell-by-cell connectome.
entries.algorithm: Development fixes priority edges. Proposed dynamics: select the highest currently active unsuppressed drive; execution reduces that drive, releasing the next program. No life weight learning is claimed. To learn a different priority graph would require an additional mechanism and rule.
entries.scaling: H = O(K) for a fixed ordered hierarchy, but up to O(K²) for an arbitrary competition graph; O(K) drive state. Work depends on graph sparsity.
entries.models: Seeds et al. (2014), eLife: hierarchical suppression model and targeted manipulations of grooming sequences. It does not demonstrate learned planning.
entries.buy: Provides a compact controller for multi-stage behavior without one dedicated parameterized layer per stage. It can also hard-code an entire solution, so developmental task leakage is a serious risk.
entries.overlap: Computational reference only. The historical screen explicitly excluded downstream motor programs from the persistent-memory core; this is not being promoted into the immediate plan.
entries.minimal_test: Priority-consistent versus edge-permuted controller with equal graph size. Measurement: completion rate of the same fixed multi-stage routine.
entries.confidence: Medium for the operational controller; low as a general learning mechanism.
entries.local_sufficiency: Not applicable to fixed sequencing; learned sequencing is unestablished.
entries.verification_status: Behavioral perturbation plus operational model; complete learned neuronal controller not demonstrated.
